questions.question: If cos x = (3)/(5), then find the value of sin x - sin³ x.
questions.solution:
Given:

Cos x = 3/5

Formula used: 

Sin x = perpendicular/hypotenuse,

Cos x = base/hypotenuse,

By Pythagoras theorem,

Hypotenuse2 = Perpendicular2 + Base2

Calculation:

According to the question:

Cos x = 3/5 

Base = 3

⇒ Hypotenuse = 5

Hypotenuse2 = Perpendicular2 + Base2

⇒ 52 = 32 + Perpendicular2

⇒ 25 = 9 + Perpendicular2

⇒ 25 – 9 = Perpendicular2

⇒ Perpendicular2 = 16

⇒ Perpendicular = √16 

⇒ Perpendicular2 = √(4 × 4)

⇒ Perpendicular = 4

Now,

(Sin x – Sin³ x)

⇒ [(perpendicular/hypotenuse) – (perpendicular/hypotenuse)³]

⇒ [4/5 – (4/5)³]

⇒ [4/5 – 64/125]

⇒ (100 – 64)/125

⇒ 36/125 = 0.288

∴ The answer is **0.288.**

questions.question: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 90 cm. If the base is 26 cm, then find the length of the equal sides.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The perimeter of an isosceles triangle = 90 cm.

And base = 26 cm

**Concept used:**

An isosceles triangle two angles will also be the same in front of the equal sides.

**Formula used:**

P = (2a + b)

Where, p = perimeter

a = side and b = another side

**Calculation:**

Let** **the length of the equal sides be x

P = (2a + b)

⇒ 90 = 2x + 26

⇒ (90 – 26) = 2x

⇒ 64 = 2x

⇒ x = 64/2 = 32

**∴ The length of the equal sides is 32 cm.**

questions.question: If sinθ = 0.96, then find cotθ
questions.solution:
Given:

sinθ = 0.96

Formula used: 

sinθ = perpendicular/hypotenuse,

cotθ = base/perpendicular

By Pythagoras theorem,

Hypotenuse2 = Perpendicular2 + Base2

Calculation:

According to the question:

sinθ = 0.96 = 96/100 = 24/25

Perpendicular = 24

⇒ Hypotenuse = 25

Hypotenuse2 = Perpendicular2 + Base2

⇒ 252 = 242 + Base2

⇒ 625 = 576 + Base2

⇒ 625 – 576 = Base2

⇒ Base2 = 49

⇒ Base = √49

⇒ Base = √(7 × 7) = 7

Now, cotθ = base/perpendicular

⇒ 7/24 = 0.2916

**∴ The value of cotθ = 0.2916.**

questions.question: The average salary of a person for the months of February, March, April, and May is Rs. 12,000, and that for the month's March, April, May June is Rs. 13,000. If his salary for the month of June is Rs. 8,000, then what is his salary for the month of February?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average salary of a person for the months of February, March, April, and May is Rs. 12,000

The month's March, April, May June is Rs. 13,000

The month of June is Rs. 8,000

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of observation/number of observation

**Calculation:**

The average salary of a person for the months of February, March, April, and May = 12000

February + March + April + May = (12000) × 4

February + March + April + May = 48000 ----(1)

Sum of the month March, April, May and June = (13000) × 4

March + April + May + June = 52000 ----(2)

Subtract from equation (1) and equation (2):-

February – June = - 4000

⇒ June salary = 8000 

⇒ February = - 4000 + 8000

February = 4000

**∴****His salary for the month of February is 4000.**

questions.question: If x³ + y³ = 16 and x + y = 4, then find the value of x⁴ + y⁴

(x + y)[(x + y)2 – 3xy]

x4 + y4 = (x2 + y2)2 – 2x2y2

**Calculation:**

(x + y)[(x + y)² – 3xy] = 16

⇒ 4[16 – 3xy] = 16

⇒ (64 – 12xy) = 16

⇒ 64 – 16 = 12xy

⇒ 48 = 12xy

⇒ [(x + y)² – 2xy]² – 2x²y²

⇒ 82 – 32

questions.question: P can do a work in 10 days and Q can do the same work in 15 days. If they work on it together for 3 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P can do a work in 10 days

Q can do the work in 15 days

**Calculation:**

Amount of work P can do in 1 day = 1/10

Amount of work Q can do in 1 day = 1/15

Amount of work P and Q can do in 1 day = 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30

Amount of work P and Q can do in 3 day = 15/30 = 1/2

Fraction of work left = 1 – 1/2 = 1/2

**∴ 1/2 of the work is left**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png] **

LCM of 10 and 15 is 30

Efficiency of P = 30/10 = 3

Efficiency of P = 30/15 = 2

Total work done by P and Q in 3 days = [(3 + 2) × 3]

⇒ 15

Remaining work = 30 – 15 = 15

Fraction of work left = 15/30 = 1/2

∴ 1/2 of the work is left

questions.question: A tradesman marks his products 35% above the cost price and allows his customers 15% reduction on their bills. What percentage of profit does he make?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A tradesman marks his products 35% above the cost price and allows his customers 15% reduction on their bills

**Formula used:**

Selling Price = Mark price - discount

Profit = selling price (S.P.) – Discount

**Calculation:**

Let Cost Price = 100

Mark Price = 100 + (100 × 35)/100 = 100 + 35 = 135

Discount is 15%

⇒ (15/100) × 135

⇒ 20.25%

Selling Price = MP - discount

⇒ 135 - 20.25

⇒ 114.75%

Profit = 114.75 - 100 = 14.75%

**∴**** Percentage of profit is 14.75%**

questions.question: A person borrows Rs. 7,000 for 3 years at 5% p.a. simple interest. He immediately lends it to another persons at 6 (1)/(3)\% p.a for 3 years. Find his gain in the transaction per year.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P₁ = 7000, T₁ = 3 year, R₁ = 5%

P₁ = 7000, T₂ = 3 year, R₂ = 6(1/3)%

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (Principal amount × rate of interest × time)/100

**Calculation:**

S.I.₁ = (P₁ × R₁ × T₁)/100

⇒ (7000 × 3 × 5)/100

⇒ 1050

S.I. for one year = 1050/3

⇒ 350

S.I.₂ = (P₁ × R₂ × T₂)/10

⇒ [7000 × (19/3) × 3]/100

⇒ 1330

S.I.₂ for one year = 1330/3

⇒ 443.33

Gain for one year = 443.33 – 350

⇒ 93.33

**∴ ****His gain in the transaction per year is 93.33**

questions.question: Two circles with the same centre P have radii 7.5 cm and 4.4 cm. Through a point A of the larger circle, a tangent is drawn to the smaller circle touching it at B and then intersecting the larger circle at C. Find AC (Approximate in cm)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two circles with the same center P have radii 7.5 cm and 4.4 cm.

A point A of the larger circle, a tangent is drawn to the smaller circle touching it at B

**Formula used:**

Using Pythagoras theorem

(Hypotenuse)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)²

Radius is perpendicular on a tangent and radius divides chords into two equal part.

**Calculation:**

In ΔABP, ∠B = 90°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/27865799dde9cda5fa858248c7770ac7e9bf79e61d8f51b9c0a2a2fca5408a9f.png] 

Using Pythagoras theorem

(AP)² = (PB)² + (AB)²

⇒ (7.5)² = (4.4)² + (x)²

⇒ 56.25 = 19.36 + x²

⇒ x² = 56.25 – 19.36

⇒ x² = 36.89

⇒ x = √36.89

⇒ x = 6.07

Length of AC = 2x = 2(6.07) = 12.14

**∴ ****Length of AC is 12.14**

questions.question: The value of 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + __________(2n - 1) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + __________(2n - 1)

**Formula used:**

Sₙ = (n/2) × [2a + (n – 1)d] = (n/2)[a + l]

**Calculation:**

First term(a) = 1,

Common difference(d) = 3 – 1 = 5 – 3 = 7 – 5 = 2

last term(l) = 2n – 1

Number of terms = n

Sum of terms = (n/2)[2a + (n – 1)d] = (n/2)[a + l]

⇒ (n/2) × (1 + 2n – 1)

⇒ (n/2) × (2n)

⇒ n × n

**∴ ****The value of 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + __________(2n - 1) is n × n**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Put n = 2

Sum of 2 term = 1 + 3 = 4

Check the option

**1.** (2n – 1)(2n – 1)

⇒ [(2 × 2) – 1][(2 × 2) – 1]

⇒ 3 × 3

⇒ 9

**2.** n/2 = 2/2 = 1

**3.** n(n + 1)/2

⇒ 2 × 3/2

⇒ 3

**4.** n × n

⇒ 2 × 2

⇒ 4

**∴ Option (4) is right.**

questions.question: Two small circular grounds of diameters 42 m and 26 m are to be replaced by a bigger circular ground. What would be the radius of the new ground if the new ground has the same area as two small grounds?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The diameter of the two small circular grounds = 42 m and 26 m respectively

**Formula Used:**

Area of the circle = πR²

**Calculation:**

The radius of the 1st circle R₁ = 42/2 = 21 m

The radius of the 2nd circle R₂ = 26/2 = 13 m 

Total Area of the two small ground = π(R²₁ + R²₂) = π ( 21² + 13²) = π × (441 + 169)

Total area = 610π m2

New ground area = 610π 

610π = πR² 

⇒ R2 = 610

⇒ R = √610

⇒ R ≈ 24.63 m

**∴ The radius of the new ground if the new ground has the same area as two small grounds is 24.63** **m.**
